title: The Doctrine of God's Love and the Anxious Heart
speaker: Steve Thomas
series: Anxiety and the Character of God

outline.title: Reframing Anxiety: Spiritual vs. Physical
subpoints: The world views anxiety as a brain-body medical issue.
Scripture identifies anxiety as a spiritual issue and a sin.
The distinction between prudent planning and sinful worry lies in the focus on God.

outline.title: The Comfort of God's Character for Believers
subpoints: Previous lessons covered God's fatherhood, aseity, omniscience, and sovereignty.
These attributes provide comfort only to those who are believers.
Unbelievers have no biblical promise that God works all things for their good.

outline.title: The Gospel as the Cure for Anxiety
subpoints: Christ reshapes the heart rather than merely removing problems.
Trials conform believers to the image of Christ.
Victory over anxiety comes through the power of Christ, not human effort.

outline.title: Defining the Nature of God's Love
subpoints: God's love is holy, forgiving, satisfying, and eternal.
It is self-sacrificial, perfect, unchanging, and steadfast.
Understanding these attributes is key to defeating anxiety.

summary:
This lesson continues a Sunday school series exploring how the doctrine of God addresses the issue of anxiety. The speaker distinguishes between the secular view of anxiety as a medical condition and the biblical perspective that frames it as a spiritual struggle. By examining the command in Matthew 6 not to be anxious, the teaching emphasizes that anxiety is a sin that is combated not by human willpower or secular coping strategies, but by meditating on the character of God.

The session reviews previous lessons on God's fatherhood, aseity, omniscience, and sovereignty, noting that these attributes offer comfort specifically to believers. It clarifies that while God promises to work all things for good for those called according to His purpose, this promise does not extend to unbelievers. The speaker highlights that the gospel is the ultimate cure for anxiety, as Christ reshapes the believer's heart and gives meaning to suffering by conforming them to His image.

The lesson concludes by defining the nature of God's love, describing it as holy, forgiving, satisfying, eternal, self-sacrificial, and steadfast. These attributes are presented as the foundation for believers to trust in God's provision and care, thereby overcoming the sin of worry and finding peace in the midst of life's trials.
